headline: Warhound emerges with $200M to genetically engineer dogs for the military
summary: Warhound, co-founded by Palmer Luckey and Ben Lamm, came out of stealth with $200 million in funding to genetically engineer dogs for military, law enforcement and first-responder use, equipping them with Anduril military gear including body armor.

claims.statement: Warhound, co-founded by Palmer Luckey and Ben Lamm, emerged from stealth with $200 million in funding to genetically engineer dogs for military, law enforcement and first-responder use.

sources.quote: Warhound, the brainchild of Ben Lamm and Palmer Luckey, emerges from stealth to genetically engineer dogs for military and law enforcement.
Warhound is genetically engineering dogs for the military, law enforcement and first responder operations.

claims.statement: Wired said Warhound aims to create elite working dogs equipped with advanced body armor.

sources.quote: elite working dogs” equipped with "advanced body armor."

claims.statement: TechCrunch said the dogs will be armed with Anduril gear.

sources.quote: Warhound raises $200M to engineer war dogs and arm them with Anduril gear

claims.statement: The Verge said Warhound is a Texas-based defense startup equipping the dogs with Anduril's military technology.

sources.quote: A new Texas-based defense startup has a plan to improve military and police dogs in the US: it's going to genetically modify them and equip them with Anduril's military technology.
